verses.text: If you see your fellow Israelite’s ox or sheep wandering off, don’t look the other way. Bring it back to them.
If the owner lives far away or you don’t know whose animal it is, take it home and keep it until the owner comes looking for it. Then give it back.
Do the same for a donkey, a piece of clothing, or anything else someone loses and you find. Don’t look the other way.
If you see your fellow Israelite’s donkey or ox collapsed by the road, don’t walk past it. Help them get it back on its feet.
A woman must not wear men’s clothes, and a man must not put on women’s clothes. Yahweh your God finds it detestable when anyone does that.
If you come across a bird’s nest in a tree or on the ground and the mother is sitting on chicks or eggs, don’t take the mother with the young.
Let the mother go. You can take the young for yourself. Then things will go well for you and you’ll live long.
When you build a new house, put a railing around the roof. That way you won’t bring guilt on your household if someone falls from there.
Don’t plant two kinds of seed in your vineyard. If you do, both the crop you planted and the produce of the vineyard will be defiled.
Don’t hitch an ox and a donkey together to plow.
Don’t wear clothes woven with wool and linen together.
Put tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wrap around yourself.
Suppose a man marries a woman, sleeps with her, and then hates her.
He brings shameful accusations against her and ruins her good name, saying, “I married this woman, but when I slept with her, I found no evidence of her virginity.”
The young woman’s father and mother will bring the evidence of her virginity to the town elders at the gate.
Her father will tell the elders, “I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he hates her.

Now he’s made this shameful accusation: ‘I found no evidence that your daughter was a virgin.’ Here’s the evidence of my daughter’s virginity.” They’ll spread the cloth out in front of the town elders.
The elders will take the man and discipline him.

They’ll fine him a hundred silver shekels and give the money to the young woman’s father, because the man ruined the good name of a virgin in Israel. She’ll remain his wife, and he can never divorce her.
But if the accusation is true and no evidence of her virginity is found,

bring the young woman to the entrance of her father’s house. The men of her town will stone her to death, because she did a disgraceful thing in Israel by acting like a prostitute in her father’s house. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from among you.
If a man is found sleeping with another man’s wife, both the man who slept with her and the woman must die. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from Israel.
Suppose a young woman who’s a virgin is engaged to be married, and a man finds her in town and sleeps with her.
Take both of them out to the town gate and stone them to death. She didn’t cry out while she was in town, and he violated his neighbor’s wife. That’s how you’ll remove the evil from among you.
But if the man finds an engaged woman out in the field and forces her to have sex with him, only the man who raped her must die.
Do nothing to the woman. She hasn’t committed a sin that deserves death. This is like someone attacking and killing their neighbor.
He found her out in the field. The engaged woman cried out, and nobody was there to save her.
If a man finds a virgin who isn’t engaged, grabs her and sleeps with her, and they’re discovered,
the man who slept with her must pay her father fifty silver shekels. She’ll become his wife because he violated her. He can never divorce her.
A man must not take his father’s wife. He must not uncover his father’s garment.
